learning_objective: 🎯 You will discover how to use special helping verbs to express ability, ask for permission, show possibility, and give advice!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Modals are superhero helping verbs! They never change their spelling for different subjects, and they do not use an 's' at the end. They change the 'mood' of the main verb to show rules, abilities, or chances.
We use 'Can' to talk about things we are able to do right now, like 'I can swim.' We use 'Could' to talk about things we were able to do in the past, like 'I could run fast when I was five.'
Want to ask politely? Use 'May', like 'May I come in?' If you are guessing that something will happen but you are not 100% sure, use 'Might', like 'It might rain today.'
If you want to give a good suggestion, use 'Should' (You should eat your vegetables). But if something is a strict rule or completely necessary, you use 'Must' (You must stop at a red light).

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Polite Request Game
fun_activity.instructions: Ask your parents for your favourite snack using the word 'May', tell them one cool thing you 'can' do, and write down one rule you 'must' follow at school!

quick_recap: ⭐ Modals are special helping verbs that do not change form.
⭐ 'May' is for polite permission, and 'Might' shows a small possibility.
⭐ 'Should' gives advice, while 'Must' shows a strong obligation or rule.
